Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 91 (further attempt): recorded a single, uncorroborated 0.9 confidence reverse geocode candidate, 3975 Heather Street, Forest Grove, OR 97116, not applied absent a second source. research_status remains complete.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Per Crane Data Centers own site, this is a multi phase campus in Forest Grove, Oregon, near Hillsboro. PDX01 Phase 1 and Phase 2 each total 36,000 square feet of white space plus 6,400 square feet of adjacent flex space at 24 MW apiece, and PDX02 adds roughly 150,000 square feet at roughly 48 MW, for a stated campus total of more than 100 MW. PDX02 is targeted ready for service in the third quarter of 2026. No street address is published on this page, and this session could not confirm how much of PDX01 is already operating versus still under construction, so critical_it_mw is left unset rather than populated from a mixed operating and planned figure. This session made a further attempt to resolve a street address. The operators own page describes the campus only as about 8 miles from Hillsboro airport, adjacent to a regional highway, still without a street number. Reverse geocoding this rows own stored coordinates through a third party service returned a single, 0.9 confidence candidate, 3975 Heather Street, Forest Grove, OR 97116, with no second, independent source confirming a Crane facility at that address. Given no second, independent source corroborates the geocoded address, it is not applied, consistent with this projects standard that a geocoding services own confidence score is not itself external corroboration.

reading.body:
Crane Data Centers is developing over 100 megawatts of capacity in the Portland metro area through a joint venture with Principal Asset Management, an institutional infrastructure investor, but the company has not published how much is currently operating versus still under construction.

The partnership structure mirrors a broader pattern in data center development where specialized operators pair with large capital providers to fund regional buildouts. Crane's emphasis on renewable energy access and site selection suggests the company is positioning around power availability, a critical constraint in the Pacific Northwest for any large AI infrastructure investment. The contested local approval process for the Forest Grove facility reflects the land use friction that large data center proposals now routinely encounter in growing metropolitan areas, even in regions with established tech industries like Oregon's Silicon Forest.

The data does not cover Crane's total company-wide capacity, headquarters location, or founding date, so the scale of this developer relative to national operators cannot be assessed from published sources. It also does not specify what portion of the announced 100+ megawatts is already serving customers or what timeline remains for the remainder of the campus build, which matters for understanding when this capacity will actually be available to consume power and support compute workloads.
